dataPoints: Williamson Act = California Land Conservation Act of 1965, Gov. Code §§51200 et seq.; restricts specific parcels to agricultural or related open-space use in exchange for property tax assessment based on farming/open-space value rather than full market value (confirmed on CA Dept. of Conservation program page).
Commercial solar is an INCOMPATIBLE use on Williamson Act-contracted land — a 100 MW solar+storage project on a contracted parcel is blocked unless the contract is exited.
Exit path 1 — Nonrenewal: 9-year phased nonrenewal (Gov. Code §51245); land remains under contract at reduced assessment for the full 9 years, so solar cannot proceed until it lapses.

Exit path 2 — Cancellation: requires payment of 12.5% of unrestricted fair market value of the land (Gov. Code §51283); 25% of unrestricted FMV if the parcel is in a Farmland Security Zone (Gov. Code §51296 et seq.).
Exit path 3 — Solar-use easement at 6.25% of unrestricted FMV, available ONLY for 'impaired' farmland; reinstated Jan 2023 by SB 1489.

CA Dept. of Conservation (DLRP) maintains the 'Williamson Act Enrollment Finder' interactive mapping tool as the authoritative parcel-level enrollment check; county Agricultural Commissioner/Assessor holds the actual contract records (contract number, enrollment date, acreage, nonrenewal/cancellation status).

Ventura County is the administering local agency for contracts within its jurisdiction; parcel-level status is confirmed via county assessor/agricultural commissioner records, not published in a scrapeable public list.
